commenti.body:
Thanks for bringing the series to my attention. There's some interesting IRL coincidences involving Nuclear plants and Conservative media that matches these releases. Especially relevant given how prevalent sex is, at least in the first film. Is it also featured in the later ones?     
   
That the 'Tall Man' is the inspiration for 'Slender Man' will no doubt be crucial in cracking open the latter's symbolism.

I adore this series. The first one will always be strongest in my heart... it captures a quiet and inky nightmarishness that no other movies really do. IV is my next favorite because it uses a bunch of clip from I which evoke that same sense of derealization. The ending is a perfect ending to the series. V is inexcusable. II and III go down a rabbit hole chasing Raimi-inspired action-comedy -- Reg essentially becomes Ash from the Evil Dead series - - and I just don't think that where Coscarelli's strengths lie.


I've written a bunch about the series on Letterboxd and I don't want to just copy-paste it all, so hopefully it's not considered too gauche to just link to my [Phantasm reviews](https://letterboxd.com/dubiouslegacy/tag/phantasm/reviews/by/added-earliest/).

Now that you mention it, and as I'm also currently playing through the Silent Hill 2 remake, the series absolutely has a Silent Hill quality to it. Especially once they elaborate on the dream world or whatever that the Tall Man is from. I think. Idk, every time I watch these movies I never get closer to what they're about.


On Shudder, the show the Last Drive in did a marathon showing all these movies and going into detail about how they were made. I recommend checking that out.


They don't have the second film because it was the only one not produced independently. But it also failed spectacularly at the box office, which is why Don ended up just keeping the rights to make his own movies.


In the late 90s, these movies played all the time on the then Sci-Fi channel.
